framework.name: Ruby on Rails
framework.overview: Rails pairs Active Record, Action Controller, and Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus) to build full-stack apps with minimal boilerplate. Master it by modeling data with migrations, writing RESTful controllers, querying with scopes, guarding input with strong params, updating the UI with Turbo Frames, and offloading work to background jobs.

challenges.title: 1. Model and migration
challenges.concept: A migration describes a schema change in Ruby; the matching Active Record model maps to that table. `create_table` defines columns and timestamps.
challenges.goal: Create an articles table (title, body) and its model.
steps: Add string :title and text :body plus t.timestamps.
hints: The model is empty; Rails infers columns.
challenges.starterCode:
class CreateArticles < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]
  def change
    # TODO: create_table :articles
  end
end

class Article < ApplicationRecord
end
challenges.solution:
class CreateArticles < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]
  def change
    create_table :articles do |t|
      t.string :title, null: false
      t.text :body
      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end

class Article < ApplicationRecord
end
challenges.expectedOutput: rails db:migrate creates the articles table

challenges.title: 2. RESTful controller action
challenges.concept: Controllers respond to routes. A RESTful `index` action loads records and renders the matching view via convention.
steps: Rely on convention to render index.html.erb.
hints: Instance variables are exposed to the view.
No explicit render needed for the default template.
challenges.starterCode:
class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def index
    # TODO
  end
end
challenges.solution:
class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def index
    @articles = Article.all
  end
end
challenges.expectedOutput: GET /articles renders the index view with all articles

challenges.title: 3. Query with a scope
challenges.concept: A `scope` names a reusable, chainable query. It returns an Active Record relation so it composes with `order`, `where`, and pagination.
challenges.goal: Add a published scope and a recent ordering scope to Article.
hints: Scopes are lambdas returning a relation.
Chaining works because each returns a relation.
challenges.starterCode:
class Article < ApplicationRecord
  # TODO: published and recent scopes
end

challenges.title: 4. Strong parameters
challenges.concept: Strong parameters allowlist attributes for mass assignment, preventing clients from setting fields you did not intend. `require` + `permit` scope the payload.
challenges.goal: Implement create with an article_params allowlist.
steps: Use it in create to build the record.
hints: require raises if the key is missing.
challenges.starterCode:
class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @article = Article.new(/* TODO */)
    if @article.save
      redirect_to @article
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  private

  # TODO: article_params
end
challenges.solution:
class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @article = Article.new(article_params)
    if @article.save
      redirect_to @article
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  private

  def article_params
    params.require(:article).permit(:title, :body)
  end
end
challenges.expectedOutput: Only :title and :body are permitted for mass assignment

challenges.title: 5. Turbo Frame partial update
challenges.concept: Hotwire's `turbo_frame_tag` scopes a region of the page. Links/forms inside a frame swap only that frame's content, giving SPA-like updates without custom JS.
challenges.goal: Wrap an article in an editable Turbo Frame.
steps: Wrap the show content with turbo_frame_tag dom_id(@article).
Add an Edit link inside the frame.
The edit response reuses the same frame id to swap in place.
hints: Matching frame ids drive the in-place swap.
challenges.starterCode:
<%# app/views/articles/show.html.erb %> <%# TODO: wrap in a turbo_frame_tag %>

<%= @article.title %>

<%= link_to "Edit", edit_article_path(@article) %>
challenges.solution:
<%# app/views/articles/show.html.erb %> <%= turbo_frame_tag dom_id(@article) do %>

<%= @article.title %>

<%= link_to "Edit", edit_article_path(@article) %> <% end %>
challenges.expectedOutput: Clicking Edit swaps only the article frame, not the whole page

challenges.title: 6. Background job
challenges.concept: Active Job abstracts background processing. Enqueue with `perform_later` so slow work (email, cleanup) runs off the request cycle via an adapter like Solid Queue.
challenges.goal: Create a job that logs a message and enqueue it after create.
hints: Pass ids, not full records, to jobs.
challenges.starterCode:
class ArticleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(article_id)
    # TODO
  end
end

# enqueue somewhere:
# TODO
challenges.solution:
class ArticleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(article_id)
    article = Article.find_by(id: article_id)
    Rails.logger.info("Cleaning up article #{article&.id}")
  end
end

# enqueue somewhere:
ArticleCleanupJob.perform_later(@article.id)
challenges.expectedOutput: perform_later pushes the job onto the queue for async execution
